claim: Moosbauer et al. (IEEE TEVC 2022 / arXiv:2111.14756) explicitly name ANOVA and functional ANOVA (fANOVA) as standard sensitivity-analysis methods, then decline them in favor of one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT)/ablation for their HPO algorithm analysis, citing OFAT's inability to detect interactions as a known limitation they accept anyway.
stance_target: N6: no prior work runs a crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial ANOVA in offline MBO
scope_conditions: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) algorithm design/explanation, YAHPO Gym surrogate benchmarks (lcbench, rbv2_super, nb301), online multi-fidelity HPO -- not offline MBO
quoted_support: "Commonly used methods are analysis of variance (ANOVA) and functional ANOVA (fANOVA) methods, which decompose the response of a (mathematical) model or function into lower-order components... We want to limit the costs of performing such a sensitivity analysis... by choosing a method that keeps the resource requirements of the experimental design reasonably low, like for example a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) analysis. Those methods have their own limitations; for example, any interactions between inputs cannot be detected by an OFAT analysis, and parts of the input space remain hidden."

claim: Moosbauer et al.'s actual RQ6 (surrogate-model effect) analysis is a one-factor-at-a-time ablation: the surrogate learner is swapped out while all other components remain fixed at the single optimized configuration gamma*, not crossed against the sampling-strategy factor (RQ5a/b) in any joint ANOVA table.
stance_target: N6: near-miss confirmed -- surrogate and search-strategy factors varied but never crossed statistically
quoted_support: "A simple method to answer many of these questions is to take the optimized configuration of Alg. 2 and swap out components of it for generally simpler components, thereby performing a one-factor-at-a-time analysis or an ablation study... RQ6 - Effect of surrogate models: ...Our ablation experiments suggest that the performance of the optimizer is on average best when using this surrogate learner, even though the differences do not seem to be significant."

claim: Full-text grep of Moosbauer et al. (19,701 words, ar5iv HTML mirror) confirms zero hits for 'factorial', 'crossed', 'eta squared'/'eta-squared', 'two-way', or 'main effect', and zero hits for 'offline' -- the paper never frames its analysis as a crossed factorial and never uses offline-MBO terminology.
stance_target: N6 near-miss confirmation: methodological gap (no factorial/ANOVA framing) and domain gap (not offline MBO) both present
scope_conditions: Full text of arXiv:2111.14756 / IEEE TEVC 26(6):1336-1350
quoted_support: Grep counts: factorial=0, crossed=0, ANOVA=5, fANOVA=2, 'analysis of variance'=1, eta squared/eta-squared=0, two-way=0, main effect=0, interaction=1, OFAT=2, one-factor-at-a-time=2, offline=0.

claim: Moosbauer et al. cite Fawcett & Hoos (ablation-path analysis in algorithm configuration, ref [42]) and a YAHPO Gym benchmark suite paper (ref [59]) as methodological antecedents, both of which are candidate leads for further citation-chasing but neither is a crossed-factorial ANOVA of surrogate x optimizer.
